newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end at record high despite BHP slide.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end at record high despite BHP slide.

text.p: The Australia share market ended with its fourth straight record close on Monday, climbing solidly in response to a Dow jump on Friday and ignoring a fall in its biggest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
The All Ordinaries Index finished up 20.9 points at 2,584.8 which was also its intra-day high and its all-time record high, eclipsing Friday's record mark of 2,572.7 by 12.1 points.
The June contract of share price index futures ended up 24 points at 2582, a 2.8 point discount to the physical index.
Turnover of A$735 million (US$653 million) was modest in comparison to recent sessions when the market has traded in excess of A$1 billion.
BHP stock sagged after the company said it expected a flat performance until it restructured its operations.
Dealers said the market could have finished 10 points higher if BHP had remained steady and up to 20 points firmer if it had pushed ahead with the market.
"There was good broad support for the market which built up as the day went along," said Jamie Spiteri, a dealer at Sydney firm, Shaw Stockbroking.
Spiteri said he expected the market to have a steady to better session on Tuesday as investors stayed on the sidelines due to holiday closures of New York and London equity markets.
Dealers said BHP's fall did, however, benefit its resource peers, as investors were seen switching into CRA Ltd and WMC Ltd stock.
CRA ended up 26.5 cents at A$21.915 (US$16.87) and WMC up 20 cents at A$8.48. BHP ended 40 cents lower at A$18.92 after touching an intra-day low of A$18.75.

Brokers said a 0.5 percentage point official interest rate cut announced on Friday also continued to affect the market with switching seen continuing to occur out of growth stocks into cyclical stocks, such as the retail and building materials and construction related stocks.

Amongst the strongest performers on the day was retailer Woolworths Ltd, whose shares ended up 17 cents at A$4.14 and building materials and sugar group, CSR Ltd which closed 14 cents higher at A$4.69.
Australia and New Zealand Banking Group was the strongest of the four major banks ahead of its half year results release on Wednesday. ANZ shares closed up 21.5 cents at A$8.53.

Pharmaceutical group F.H. Faulding & Co was among the few weaker issues on the day as investors factored in possible negative effects on earnings caused by changes made by the government to subsidies for prescription drugs.
